content.title: About
content.content: Oatmeal is a ready‑to‑eat product made from whole oat grains, designed for fast preparation in fast‑food settings. It is typically steamed, dried and flavored with varieties such as berry, chocolate or vanilla.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 5,000 years.
Instant oatmeal is often fortified with B‑vitamins and iron.
Flavorings can be natural (berries, nuts) or artificial, but always pass safety checks.
Oatmeal in fast‑food is commonly served in single‑serve cups for on‑the‑go convenience.
Oats contain beta‑glucans, which help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Oatmeal provides soluble fiber that supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Lowers cholesterol
items.content: Beta‑glucans in oats can reduce LDL (bad) cholesterol.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: It delivers steady energy without rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Contains vitamins and minerals
items.content: Includes B1, magnesium, iron and zinc, important for metabolism.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Regular oatmeal consumption is linked to a reduced risk of heart disease.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oats or added flavorings.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Flavored versions often contain added sugars, increasing calorie count.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats can be contaminated with wheat during processing, so people with celiac disease should choose certified gluten‑free options.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Convenient portion sizes can lead to eating more than recommended, potentially causing weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the oatmeal in the microwave or with hot water for 1–2 minutes, then add fruit, nuts, honey or yogurt. It can be used as a quick breakfast, snack, or dessert base.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool place away from direct light. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and consume within 2–3 days.
